transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-29
Start: 16:30 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Rourke (Redwood SE), Ravi Patel (Edenware CTO), Sofia Martinez (ML Engineer), Harper Lee (PM), Jordan Kim (Infra)

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, we're on for 50 minutes, just a quick agenda; scope success criteria, workload and load numbers, golden prompts, regression, then next steps. can we do a quick round-robin?
[00:15] Ravi Patel: yeah ravi here, appreciate it. we're trying to pilot a chat summarization + ticket triage flow inside edenware's support portal. main concerns latency and hallucinations because legal needs low false positives.
[00:30] Harper Lee: Harper — product, we want the pilot to demonstrate 3 things: 1) accuracy on triage labels >= 92% on our golden set, 2) <5% hallucination rate on summaries, 3) median p95 latency under 420ms for 256 token responses.
[00:50] Maya Chen: great concrete targets, that's helpful. liam any initial notes on feasibility?
[00:58] Liam O'Rourke: yeah quick note — those latency numbers are tight but doable with Redwood Dedicated or optimized hosted instance + prefix caching. we'll want to know typical prompt lengths, avg response length, and concurrency spike patterns. also need to confirm whether you want private deployment (VPC) for the datacenter or if hosted is acceptable for the pilot.
[01:20] Jordan Kim: infra — private VPC preferred for eval, we have egress controls and internal KMS; can we do VPC peering? Also the team is worried about sustained throughput: our peak concurrent users ~180 active sessions, avg qps ~40, burst to 220 for short windows.
[01:40] Maya Chen: noted. standard approach is we run the benchmark in your VPC via the Redwood Private connector or spin up dedicated capacity in our hosted env routed through a secure tunnel. we'll outline both options.
[01:55] Sofia Martinez: on the data side i'll prepare 250 examples and mark the golden labels; also we have 50 edge cases that historically trip models — sarcasm, nested tickets. we'll provide them but they may need masking.
[02:10] Ravi Patel: timeline? we'd like a pilot contract green by mid-august and testing complete by end of september.
[02:20] Maya Chen: tall order but possible. proposed pilot timeline: week 0 (now): kickoff & data share; week 1–2: golden prompt creation and initial runs; week 3: regression testing and hallucination analysis; week 4: full load benchmark; week 5–6: final acceptance & metrics review.
[02:40] Harper Lee: sounds fine. can you explain how you recommend building the golden prompts? we don't want to bias them too much.
[02:50] Liam O'Rourke: sure — golden prompts should be representative across buckets (happy path, edge, ambiguous). we recommend 150–200 gold prompts for classification + 50–100 for free-text summarization checks. prompts should include both short and long context. we'll help author an initial set based on your 250 examples.
[03:15] Sofia Martinez: good. and regression tests? do you do automated regression across model versions?
[03:22] Liam O'Rourke: yes, recommended flow: baseline run on current model -> record golden-set outputs and scores -> on any model change run regression suite and compute delta. we store outputs and diff metrics; threshold triggers a manual review if delta in accuracy > 2% or hallucination rate increases > 1.5%.
[03:45] Ravi Patel: how do you define hallucination? we have strict legal definitions — any fabricated assertions about customer data are unacceptable.
[03:52] Maya Chen: we use a two-step definition: content hallucination when model asserts facts not present in prompt or dataset, and format hallucination when it violates required output schema (e.g., missing JSON fields). For your legal bar we'll set a stricter tolerance — propose 1% allowable content hallucination on the golden set and zero tolerance for format violations on structured outputs. Thoughts?
[04:18] Harper Lee: zero tolerance for format errors is a must for our downstream parsers.
[04:22] Liam O'Rourke: we'll instrument schema checks with automated parsers and qty percentage of outputs auto-fail if JSON doesn't parse. format checks will be part of the CI regression.
[04:35] Jordan Kim: SSO and audit logs — we need user-level audit, SAML SSO, and KMS integration for keys. does Redwood Private support customer-managed keys?
[04:45] Maya Chen: yes, Private supports KMS/HSM integrations and we can enable customer-managed keys. audit logs are exportable to your SIEM; we'll share SOC2 and ISO paperwork.
[04:56] Ravi Patel: competitors — we've looked at MegaAI and CloudServe; our infra team found their latency inconsistent at scale. that's why we're interested in Redwood's batching and KV cache approach.
[05:10] Liam O'Rourke: quick technical detail: KV cache warmup matters for p95. our benchmark will include a warmup phase with realistic session continuity and evaluate both cold-start and warm-state latencies.
[05:30] Sofia Martinez: for scoring approach what metrics do you recommend beyond accuracy/hallucination/latency?
[05:37] Liam O'Rourke: recommended primary metrics: classification accuracy (macro and micro), hallucination rate (content + format), latency distribution (p50/p95/p99), and stability (variance across runs). secondary: token costs per session and model throughput. For acceptance gate propose weighted score: 50% accuracy, 25% hallucination penalty (lower is better), 15% latency score, 10% stability. overall pass threshold 80/100.
[06:05] Ravi Patel: can you give an example of how that weighting translates to a pass/fail?
[06:10] Liam O'Rourke: sure — accuracy 92% -> 46 points, hallucination rate 1% -> 23 points (we invert so lower creates higher score), latency p95 400ms -> 12 points, stability -> 8 points, total 89 -> pass. we'll provide the scoring spreadsheet with formulas.
[06:30] Harper Lee: what about regression acceptance? do we allow slight drops if latency improves?
[06:35] Maya Chen: tradeoffs are acceptable but must be explicit in the SOW. we can set rollback thresholds and canary windows — e.g., allow accuracy drop up to 1% only if hallucination rate decreases and latency improves by 10%. We'll document policy.
[06:55] Ravi Patel: we want the golden set to be blinded during evaluation so that the team can't overfit. can Redwood support sequestering the golden set?
[07:02] Liam O'Rourke: yes we recommend a holdout golden set stored in your account; SEs run evaluation on it and share aggregate metrics only. optionally we can host the eval runner in your VPC so data never leaves.
[07:20] Harper Lee: ok let's talk throughput numbers for load testing. we mentioned 40 qps average, 220 bursts — how do you prefer to simulate that?
[07:28] Liam O'Rourke: we'll run phased load profile: baseline 40 qps for 30 minutes, ramp to 180 qps over 10 minutes, bursts at 220 qps for 2-minute intervals repeated 5 times. measure p95/p99 and error rate. include steady-state test for 1 hour for resource stability.
[07:50] Jordan Kim: what about token lengths? typical user prompts avg 120 tokens, responses avg 220 tokens, sometimes 600 tokens for long threads. we need measurements for 256 and 512 windows.
[08:05] Liam O'Rourke: noted — benchmark runs will include 128/256/512 response windows. we'll capture memory usage and throughput. For on-prem we may tune quantization profiles; we'll propose configs after initial runs.
[08:25] Sofia Martinez: on hallucination detection — do you use automated classifiers or human labels?
[08:30] Liam O'Rourke: hybrid approach: automated heuristics (fact-checker against known data sources, entity mismatch detectors) + human spot-check for edge cases. for pilot we'll sample 10% human review on flagged outputs.
[08:45] Harper Lee: curious about regression test cadence — how often do you rerun tests in production?
[08:50] Maya Chen: recommended weekly automated smoke runs for core flows and full regression on any model update or infra change. for pilot we will run full suite after each tuning iteration.
[09:05] Ravi Patel: can you show a simple acceptance checklist now?
[09:10] Maya Chen: yes quick checklist: 1) Accuracy >= 92% on golden-set classification, 2) Content hallucination <= 1% on golden summaries, 3) Format errors = 0% for structured outputs, 4) p95 latency <= 420ms in warm cache state, 5) Sustained 40 qps and burst handling to 220 qps with error rate <1%, 6) Audit logs and KMS integration verified. If all pass -> pilot acceptance.
[09:45] Harper Lee: that maps well to our needs. one more question: what's your recommended size for the regression suite overall?
[09:52] Liam O'Rourke: baseline regression: 1k classification examples split across buckets + 200 summarization golden samples. but for pilot start smaller (500 + 100) then expand. goal is coverage across ticket types.
[10:05] Ravi Patel: sounds good. any legal/compliance docs you need to start?
[10:12] Maya Chen: we'll send the Redwood SOC2 pack and our standard DPA; if you need an addendum for data residency we'll escalate. also we'll include a security runbook for the benchmark.
[10:25] Harper Lee: final ask — can you provide an example scoring sheet and a demo of the regression dashboard?
[10:30] Liam O'Rourke: yes we'll share a scoring spreadsheet and schedule a 30-minute demo of the dashboard next week.
[10:38] Maya Chen: ok recap on next steps and owners, then wrap.
[10:45] Ravi Patel: thanks everyone, excited to run this.

[11:00] End of recording.

Notes on transcription: occasional misattributions, "Redwood dedicate" heard in one spot, some punctuation missing.

Bench plan appendix (brief):
- Golden prompts: Rdw + Edenware co-author 200 classification + 75 summarization, golden holdout 80 classification + 25 summarization.
- Regression policy: run full suite on each model variant; auto-block if accuracy delta > 2% or hallucination delta > 1.5%.
- Benchmark config: 128/256/512 seq windows; cold/warm runs; warmup 15 minutes; load phases as above.
- Scoring formula: weighted score spreadsheet (50% accuracy, 25% hallucination invert, 15% latency, 10% stability) with pass >=80.

References shared during call:
- Golden prompts template: https://drive.redwood.example/edenware/golden-prompts-template.xlsx
- Pilot SOW template: https://drive.redwood.example/pilot/sow-template.pdf
- Security pack snapshot: https://redwood.example/security/soc2-brief.pdf

Caveats: transcription imperfect; numeric thresholds need formalization in SOW.
